The long train of freight cars whined
and grumbled as it strove to stop. In
the doorway of a great low building a
white capped and gowned woman re
leased a sunny smile and, turning so
her voice carried into the building,
called out, "They are ours; get ready
for a rush."
Just how she could tell they were
"ours" would be hard to explain, for
at the moment she spoke hundreds of
the dirtiest, grizzliest men a woman
ever saw came fairly tumbling out of
the freight cars. A moment more she
was welcoming this muddy rabble with
a laugh and cheering words.

RED CROSS CAMPAIGN
OBION COUNTY FOR $10,000
Funds for work of the American
Red Cross must be recruited. Dr.
Turner, the couaty chairman, is
making preparations for the organi
zation of his work here. Everybody
must be prepared to do his bit, and
everybody has some duty to perform.
The Red Cross work is a part of this
duty. The campaign in the county
must have more encouragement and
support than heretofore, notwith
standing the fact that it has been
altogether successful. The work is
larger all the time and the needs are
greater. m There is every indication
that the support of the work in the
county will be more liberal. People
here are realizing more than ever
the importance of, every branch of
the war work. They are beginning
to drop per8onaljfeelings in the mat
ter of organization and to concen
trate their efforts. Obion County
must stand as a unit, shoulder to
shoulder, and get under this work.
It must be done and can be well
done only thru united effort.

organization to conduct the work in

In announcing the various com
mittees for the. great oncoming cam
paign, to raise our proportionate
part of the" $100,000,000, I have
done so with the hope that every
member of the committees will re
alize that upon him or her depends
the success or failure of the cam
paign, and that the committees as
appointed, will not shirk, criticise,
or ask to be relieved of any respon
sibility We all realize that the de
mands upon the people at this time
are great and continuous, both for
time and money, but what do we
care for time and money during such
a crisis, when the war is at this
acutely critical stage, and when
those hounds of infamy the Huns
are drinking toasts to the time of
their arrival in America? I am sure
you people of Obion County have
heard the trumpet call, and that you
will rally, as you always have, going
over the top with credit to your
selves and the great cause to which
you are asked to respond
Speakers will appear In each town
ship and thickly settled parts of each
district during the week of the cam
paign, May 20-27. Please hear all
the speaking you can, and thus re
ceive a message full of that knowl
edge and pariotism so necessary to
every American at this time.

Planning High Corn Yields.
Good seed corn Is scarce this year.
Inspect each ear and if possible test
it to see if it will germinate. A
good stand is essential to a good
yield." Plant pure seed.
Be sure that the soil is well pre
pared first. Plant on the level or in
shallow rows.
If a crust forms or weeds come,
cross harrow the field before the corn
is up and then again as soon as it
is up and grass appears. Three such
harrowings are usually needed?
Honor Flag.
Mr, Harris Parks, chairman of the
Third Liberty Loan organization in
Obion County, received notice in a
letter Wednesday that Obion County
had been placed in the list of coun
ties winning an honor flag for her
subscriptions to the Third Libertjr
Loan. This, of course, required a
minimum of 235,000 and a number
subscribers equal to seven and one
half per cent of the population of
the cpunty. The total amount "sub
scribed was $420,000 and the num
ber of subscribers was 2,450. This
flag will be presented with the prop
er ceremonies to the County Court
by Mr. Parks at the July term of
court.
Obion County salesmen secured
subscriptions in Obion County for
the above amount. Some sixty
thousand. of this, however, will be
placed to the credit of border coun
ties where it will be banked. But
the total represents the amount suh
scribed by citizens of Obion County,
and the chairman, Mr. Parks, de
serves to be complimented and con
gratulated for the excellence of his.
organization. It wa3 freely pre
dieted by leading citizens that the
minimum of the loan would be hard
to get In the county. Those of us,
however, who wore initiated into the
plans, differed from that view. It
was practically easy. It depended,
however, on the organization, and
Mr. Parks saw to it that this was
properly handled.
Obion County i3 over the topr,
thanks to Mr. Parks and every mem
ber of his organization.
